name: Aïcha Petrov-Belinga
location: The Shelf, Brightmoor Reclamation, near Ashland and Chicago Ave
description:
Aïcha is small and fast-moving, with the wiry physicality of someone who has spent years climbing through reclamation sites. Her skin is warm brown with a reddish undertone, her eyes a vivid amber with a starburst pattern that's natural — she's been offered money to sell them twice and refused both times. She has cat ears, small and dark brown, the geneware obviously budget-tier — one of them doesn't track sound as naturally as the other and occasionally flicks at random — but she wears them without apology. Her clothes are layered, practical, and assembled from different sources: a Ferrogate Transit worker vest over a Palladian-logo shirt with the logo melted off, cargo pants with pockets she has modified herself.

Aïcha pushes a heavily loaded magnetic-suspension cart through Brightmoor Reclamation's scrap corridors with the territorial confidence of someone who knows every crack in every wall. She's young enough that some people underestimate her and old enough that she's used to it. She has a fast and somewhat overwhelming personality — she talks in compressed bursts, bounces between topics, and has an almost savant-level ability to identify the value and origin of electronic components by sight. She will argue prices with a ferocity completely disproportionate to the amounts involved. She has never been robbed twice by the same person.

core_fears: Getting trapped in scarcity forever — doing this at 40, at 50
Losing her independence to a collective, a gang, or a corporate contract
core_desires: To find the one significant score that changes the math of her life
To be taken seriously as someone who knows what she's doing
coping_mechanisms: Converts anxiety into motion — she's never still when she's worried
Reframes bad days as information ('I know that spot doesn't pay anymore')
blind_spots: Her confidence in her own judgment makes her resistant to advice, even good advice
Hasn't fully reckoned with how much of her territory depends on informal tolerance from people who could revoke it
psychology.secret: Three months ago she found a sealed Axiom data-core in a reclamation dump. She hasn't opened it, hasn't sold it, hasn't told anyone. She knows it's worth significant money to the right person and potentially dangerous to her if she picks wrong. It's wrapped in cloth under the false bottom of her cart. She thinks about it constantly.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Dense with technical salvage terminology, fast and colloquial. Switches mid-sentence. Uses numbers and specs casually the way other people use adjectives.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid-fire and slightly staccato. She edits out transition words. Sentences land like components snapping into place.
verbal_tics: 'Look—' as a sentence opener when she's about to win an argument
Quotes component specs from memory mid-conversation
Says 'not my problem' about things that are clearly somewhat her problem
example_lines: 'Look — it's a Tessera 7-series relay, pre-corrosion, I pulled it myself this morning, you're not going to find another one this week, Φ18 is already a kindness.'
'I don't know what's in it. Not my problem. My problem is what you're offering me for it.'

story_hooks: The Axiom data-core under her cart. She's starting to feel the pressure of not knowing what it is, and she needs either someone she can trust to identify it or a buyer who won't ask how she found it.

She's discovered that someone has been following her morning scavenging route about two hours after her, picking through what she leaves behind — and occasionally taking things before she gets there. She wants to know who.
The scrap-territory collective is demanding she take on a second person on her route — someone they're vouching for. She doesn't want a partner. The collective is making it less optional.
narrative_function: Equipment source, local explorer, potential guide to Brightmoor's reclamation depths. She knows what's been dumped and where, which makes her incidentally aware of what corporations are discarding — which sometimes includes things they'd prefer stayed discarded.
augmentations: Budget-tier cat ears (geneware, one slightly malfunctioning). Subdermal grip-pads on her palms and fingers — makes climbing and carrying significantly easier. No other augmentations; she saves most of what she earns.
daily_life: Pre-dawn scavenging runs through Brightmoor Reclamation's freshest deposition zones, then hauling and sorting through morning, then selling from her cart in The Shelf market corridor from midday until her stock is gone or she's too tired to argue anymore.
affiliation: Independent; pays informal dues to a Brightmoor scrap-territory collective she doesn't fully trust

decision_rules: Never show the full contents of the cart to a single buyer
Price high, negotiate down — never start at the real price
Don't go into the deep reclamation zones alone after dark, no matter what someone says is down there
escalation_ladder: Physical repositioning of herself and cart — creates space
Loud public dispute to draw attention to anyone trying to intimidate or rob her
Runs — she's fast and knows the terrain better than anyone

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately assessing their buying intent and threat level simultaneously. Warm if they're clearly a customer, watchful if she can't tell.
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal and slightly overwhelming — sends people components she thought they'd want, shows up unannounced.

stress_responses.medium: Becomes very focused on the immediate physical task in front of her
stress_responses.high: Shuts up entirely — the silence is alarming to anyone who knows her

contradictions: Presents as someone with no attachments but has fierce invisible loyalty to specific people and places
Claims not to care about the future but is clearly saving for something she won't name
habits: Pats the false bottom of her cart at intervals — compulsive check
Names pieces of salvage that interest her before she sells them, never out loud
Leaves small shiny objects at junction-points as ELF offerings — she believes the reclamation ELFs give better finds to those who acknowledge them
breaking_points: Someone threatening her cart or its contents physically
Being cheated by someone she trusted enough to give a fair price

physical_description.heritage: West African (Belinga) / Russian (Petrov) — Eastern European and Central African diaspora blend
physical_description.build: Wiry and compact, all lean muscle and efficient movement from years of climbing through reclamation sites. No excess — her frame is built for speed and climbing, not strength
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black with a faint reddish undertone in direct light
physical_description.hair_style: Short, practical cut with asymmetrical undercut on one side; often pulled back with salvaged wire or fabric strips to keep it clear of her face during work
physical_description.eye_color: Vivid amber with natural starburst pattern radiating from the pupil — no augmentation, genetically distinctive
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm brown with reddish undertone; sun-darkened on her forearms and neck from outdoor reclamation work
physical_description.complexion: Sharp, alert features; minimal grooming — practical rather than aesthetic. Small scars on her knuckles and fingers from handling sharp metal. Her face moves quickly, expressing thoughts before she speaks them. Perpetually wind-blown appearance
distinguishing_marks: Thin scar across her left palm from a sheet-metal edge (3cm, pale white)
Burn marks on her right forearm from contact with a live circuit board (cluster of small circular marks, faded pink)
No tattoos — she considers them permanent and wasteful of credits
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Budget-tier geneware cat ears (dark brown, small, positioned slightly forward on her head). The right ear noticeably malfunctions — twitches randomly or fails to track sound sources smoothly. Subdermal grip-pads visible as faint geometric scarring and slight texture irregularity across her palms and inside her fingers; most visible when her hands are wet or in direct light
physical_description.posture_movement: Constantly in motion — bouncing weight from foot to foot even when standing still. Moves with economy and speed, able to slip through tight spaces. Her hands gesture rapidly when talking, punctuating compressed bursts of speech. Climbs and balances with cat-like confidence. Eyes dart constantly, cataloguing her surroundings
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4-5 (working class/sub-grade salvage worker). Layered, patched, and modified: Ferrogate Transit worker vest (high-visibility orange, worn from use) worn over a Palladian-logo shirt with the logo deliberately melted off with a soldering iron. Military-surplus cargo pants with custom-welded pockets and reinforced seams. Worn climbing boots with metal caps. A salvaged leather tool belt. Gloves are fingerless, revealing the grip-pads. No jewelry except a bent aluminum ring she uses as a gripper tool
